title: Introduce namespace quarantine and idempotent secret-sync init flow for private upgrades
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an opt-in namespace quarantine mechanism for Private upgrades and an idempotent secret-sync init job to reduce race conditions during tenant onboarding and upgrades. Default disabled; opt-in via values. Backwards compatible.
body:
Context and motivation:
Private deployments deploy to customer-controlled clusters where multiple tenant namespaces and on-prem automation can cause racey upgrades. We saw two classes of failures in recent canaries: 1) concurrent post-upgrade controllers touching shared secrets during init causing conflicts and transient errors that delayed rollouts, and 2) partial upgrades where tenant workloads started before critical init steps completed. This PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in 'namespace quarantine' annotation plus an idempotent secret-sync init flow to make preupgrade/init steps more deterministic and safe for rollback.

What this PR changes (single-line description):
- Add values schema fields to control namespace quarantine and secret-sync retry policy.
- Add templated pre-upgrade 'quarantine' hook that marks namespaces with a quarantine annotation and prevents sidecars/controllers from processing tenant traffic during init.
- Introduce a Kubernetes Job template 'secret-sync' that applies secrets using a create-or-update idempotent approach with exponential backoff and leader-affinity for multi-replica installs.
- Add a corresponding post-upgrade hook to remove quarantine and do a graceful unquarantine probe.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Schema: added values.schema.json validations for new fields and defaults.
- [x] Templates: new hooks/secret-sync-job.yaml and hooks/namespace-quarantine-hook.yaml.
- [x] Tests: unit template snapshots + integration helm template with sample values.
- [x] Documentation: added notes to CHARTS_UPGRADE.md about opt-in behavior and troubleshooting.
- [x] CI: added a smoke helm template CI job for private-installer charts.

Commits (high level):
- feat(quarantine): add values schema and defaults for quarantine and secret-sync retry policy
- feat(hooks): implement pre-upgrade namespace quarantine hook and post-upgrade unquarantine hook
- feat(init): add secret-sync job template with idempotent apply logic and retry policy
- test: snapshot updates and helm template smoke tests

Files touched (high-level):
- charts/private/values.schema.json (added new keys: quarantine.enabled, quarantine.annotationKey, secretSync.enabled, secretSync.retryPolicy, secretSync.timeoutSeconds)
- charts/private/templates/hooks/namespace-quarantine-hook.yaml (new pre/post hooks)
- charts/private/templates/hooks/secret-sync-job.yaml (new init job template)
- charts/private/templates/_helpers.tpl (utility funcs for annotation keys and leader labels)
- charts/private/CHARTS_UPGRADE.md (docs)
- tests/helm/smoke/private-quarantine-values.yaml (test values)

Implementation notes and design decisions:
- Opt-in by default: quarantine.enabled = false. We intentionally avoid turning this on automatically for existing customers.
- Annotation-based quarantine: the hook applies an annotation (configurable key) to selected tenant namespaces. The operator and sidecars are expected to watch this annotation; we include non-invasive annotation semantics so older components ignore it.
- Idempotent secret-sync: the job uses a small init container that runs a controlled kubectl/helm-based apply (create-if-not-exists; patch-if-different). We implemented a deterministic merge strategy for secret data keys to avoid stomping operator-managed fields.
- Retry/backoff policy: secretSync.retryPolicy supports simple backoff parameters (initialIntervalSeconds, multiplier, maxIntervalSeconds, maxElapsedSeconds). The job exits 0 when all secrets are applied or when timeout is exceeded and leaves a status ConfigMap to be reconciled by the operator.
- Leader affinity: in multi-replica chart installs the job is scheduled with a leader label selector and a pre-hook leader-elector helper to avoid concurrent secret writes.
- Safe rollback behavior: quarantine is removed in the post-upgrade hook only after health probes succeed. If the release is rolled back, the pre-hook teardown is idempotent and leaves namespaces in their previous state.

Template examples (excerpt):
values.schema.json snippet:
{
  "properties": {
    "quarantine": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {"type": "boolean", "default": false},
        "annotationKey": {"type": "string", "default": "redwood.io/quarantine"}
      }
    },
    "secretSync": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {"type": "boolean", "default": true},
        "retryPolicy": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "initialIntervalSeconds": {"type": "integer", "default": 5},
            "multiplier": {"type": "number", "default": 2.0},
            "maxIntervalSeconds": {"type": "integer", "default": 60},
            "maxElapsedSeconds": {"type": "integer", "default": 300}
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Operational notes for operators:
- To enable for a tenant during a staged upgrade, set quarantine.enabled=true and target namespaces with labels selector: charts.private.quarantine.selector. The pre-hook will run and annotate namespaces before secret-sync runs.
- Monitor the job by watching the secret-sync ConfigMap status and Helm hook logs. For troubleshooting, CHARTS_UPGRADE.md includes a small debug snippet for re-running the job manually.
- The annotation key can be customized to avoid conflicts with existing on-prem policies. The operator will ignore unknown keys by default.

Review conversation (high level):
- Daniel Park (reviewer): Requested stronger validation on the retryPolicy defaults to avoid infinite loops. Also asked for explicit timeouts on the Job spec.
- Author (Maya Chen): Added maxElapsedSeconds validation and Job activeDeadlineSeconds tunable. Updated values.schema.json and templates to surface default timeouts.
- Ethan Zhao (reviewer): Requested a non-invasive default for leader-election that falls back to node-affinity if the leader label helper isn't present. Updated helper template and documented fallback behavior.
- Priya Nair (reviewer): Asked for a short note in CHARTS_UPGRADE.md explaining how this interacts with existing migrate hooks; added a compatibility section.
- Final: approvals from Daniel and Priya after the above changes.

CI and merge status:
- CI: Helm lint, template parse, unit snapshot tests, and the new smoke job ran and passed. One transient lint failure required a fix for a missing tpl helper; rerun passed.
- Merge: squash and merge into main after approvals.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default off: no behavior changes for existing installs.
- Documented opt-in steps in CHARTS_UPGRADE.md and sample values in tests/helm.
- Recommend enabling quarantine for high-concurrency tenant onboarding or large on-prem clusters where secret churn caused issues.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-8810):
- Operator-side: add a more robust probe that checks service readiness across split clusters.
- Metrics: emit quarantine lifecycle metrics so SRE can monitor time spent in quarantine per tenant.
- UX: add Console guidance if Private installer detects on-prem clusters with many tenant namespaces.

If you'd like I can split the secret-sync job into a small controller in a follow-up to avoid Job re-runs being long-lived in the cluster, but for this PR keeping it as a Job keeps the change small and easier to backport to older chart branches.

Signed-off-by: Maya Chen
